name: Markdown

props.description: Host markers (callouts, embeds), run after GFM. Their output is still sanitised — allow marker attributes with `schema`.
props.name: remarkPlugins

props.description: Tags / attributes a host plugin needs. A rule for an attribute the base already constrains is MERGED into it (e.g. `code` `className` + `math-inline`), gh#1116. It can never widen the URL policy or bring raw HTML back.
props.name: schema

props.description: Map a host scheme (`asset:…`, wiki links) to a real URL. Runs BEFORE the sanitiser, which then judges the result.
props.name: resolveUrl

props.description: Server-assigned anchors instead of GitHub slugs.
props.name: headingId

props.description: Element overrides (react-markdown). Mermaid fences are drawn through the gate BEFORE a host `pre` is asked, so a host code renderer keeps Mermaid (gh#1116).
props.name: components

props.description: Run AFTER the sanitiser — presentation only.
props.name: rehypePlugins

props.description: Narrow the elements a body may produce (with `unwrapDisallowed` to keep their text) — an activity feed showing only strong / em / del / code. Only removes; never allows what the schema strips (gh#1116).
props.name: allowedElements

props.description: A table cell whose trimmed text has no whitespace and at most this many characters (grapheme clusters) — a code, an id, a date, 優先度 — is stamped data-short, and Prose keeps it on one line (CJK otherwise breaks between ideographs in a narrow column). Sentences still wrap. false stamps nothing (gh#1150). Images in Prose table cells are capped at --prose-cell-image-max-inline-size (20rem) so a narrow table scrolls instead of squashing them.
props.name: shortCellLength

props.description: Default 'same-tab'. Renderer policy for links to another origin (an absolute http(s) URL whose origin differs from `origin`). 'new-tab' adds target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer"; relative links, #anchors, resolved wikilinks and mailto: stay in the tab. Markdown cannot store target, so this replaces it.
props.name: externalLinks

props.description: The page origin externalLinks compares against; defaults to location.origin. Pass it for server rendering, or every absolute link counts as external there.
props.name: origin

props.description: Visible titles for GitHub-alert callouts (`> [!WARNING]`) that carry none of their own. English by default (the package has no i18n); pass localized strings. Grammar v1 (gh#1156): callouts, `:::toggle[summary]`, `::::columns`/`:::column{width=N}`, CJK-friendly emphasis — the same syntax the pure codec at `@godxjp/markdown/codec` (CODEC_ID kit-md@2, parse/serialize/normalize, DOM-free) and @godxjp/block-editor use.
props.name: calloutTitles

props.description: `false` keeps ```mermaid fences as code. Diagrams need the optional peer `mermaid`.
props.name: mermaid

props.description: Fenced code in a known language is tokenised at parse time as `<span data-code-token>` with the kit's twelve names, which Prose colours (renderer v6). `false` leaves plain text for a host `pre` with its own highlighter.
props.name: highlight

props.description: Host renderers for container directives the kit does not model, by name (`{ poll: (b) => <PollCard … /> }`). Each gets `{ name, label, attributes, source, body, children }` — label / source / body as written, `children` the rendered body without the label (a `::::form`'s `:::poll` cards). Return `undefined` to render the block as an unknown directive (its content in `div.ui-prose-directive`), which is also what an unregistered name renders. `toggle` / `columns` / `column` cannot be overridden.
props.name: directives

related: Prose — the typography wrapper this renders into.
MarkdownEditor — editing; its preview is this renderer.
CodeBlock — a single block of preformatted text, not a document.
tagline: The one Markdown renderer for GoDX apps (sibling package `@godxjp/markdown`, versioned with the kit): GFM + GitHub heading anchors, one sanitiser schema (no raw HTML; http/https/mailto/relative URLs only), and ```mermaid drawn only after its SVG passes a fail-closed gate (gh#1108). Wrap it in `Prose`.
usage: DO let the document language do Japanese line breaking: under `:lang(ja)` (AppProvider sets `<html lang>`) every prose paragraph and list item breaks between PHRASES — `word-break: auto-phrase` + `line-break: strict`, the `Text break="phrase"` behaviour (gh#1310) — so 「新しく参加」 is not cut 「新し｜く参加」. Latin and Vietnamese wrap unchanged; a phrase longer than the line still breaks inside itself. A browser without `auto-phrase` keeps its own CJK breaking.

Table of contents: outline(markdown) from @godxjp/markdown/codec returns { depth, text, id }[] with exactly the ids <Markdown> writes — feed it to the kit Anchor. YAML front matter is kept verbatim and never rendered; frontmatterOf(markdown) returns it (gh#1163).
DO `<Prose><Markdown>{body}</Markdown></Prose>` for every rendered body (wiki page, issue, mail).
DO record `MARKDOWN_FORMAT` and `RENDERER_VERSION` on stored versions.

DO `import "@godxjp/markdown/katex.css"` once in the app: `$…$`, `$$…$$` and ```math are drawn by KaTeX at parse time (trust: false, renderer v6) and need its stylesheet and fonts. A single `$` follows Pandoc's rule, so `$5 and $10` stays text.

DO import `Markdown` from `@godxjp/markdown/lazy` in a client-rendered app: KaTeX (+ its stylesheet, no global katex.css import needed) and highlight.js load only when a body has math or a fence with a language, then the body re-renders. The default entry stays eager because a server or Worker render is synchronous; a server or a hydrating client using `/lazy` awaits `preloadMarkdownRuntime(body)` first.
DON'T assemble react-markdown + rehype-sanitize per app, add rehype-raw, or render Mermaid yourself — `checkMermaidSvg` is the gate.
